name: Sprocket
text: Do A/B test prompt hashing on 1% traffic for one week. Hashing catches rewording that silently changes behavior without new tests. Trade-off: 1% risk of bad responses for faster detection of prompt drift.

name: Gauge
text: Hashing only flags exact rewordings—semantic drift slips through undetected. A 1% traffic slice risks bad responses without solving the core problem: we still need human review for meaning changes. Instead, run a controlled prompt variant audit: log all prompt changes, flag semantic shifts with a lightweight LLM check, and auto-revert only if the drift score crosses a threshold. Settle it with a week-long pilot comparing drift detection accuracy against the hashing baseline.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: A weekly audit still misses drift that happens *between* audits—users get bad responses in real time. Instead, run a dual system: log *all* prompt changes instantly, but only auto-apply if they pass a fast semantic diff check (e.g., embeddings + human triage for edge cases).
